nav.spots.sub: Who is on the air from a park
cfg.title: Settings
cfg.calls.p: Save as many as you use; pick one when you start recording.
cfg.calls.err: A callsign is letters, digits and / only.
cfg.calls.last: The last callsign cannot be removed.
cfg.p2p.auto: When a spot shows the other station's park, record it as P2P without asking
cfg.p2p.p: Off: each QSO asks yes / no. Either way the other side's upload (hunter log), when known, wins at build time.
live.title: Which park today?
live.lede: Start recording when you go on the air. Stations spotted from parks are noted every minute, so P2P and 2fer can still be worked out after they go QRT.
live.err.park: Enter the park reference like JP-1266.
live.qsoNote.left: {n} more QSOs to complete the activation
live.qsosEmpty1: Waiting for QSOs from the logger.
live.deleted: QSO with {call} was deleted in the logger
live.finishPending: {n} QSOs may be P2P and are unconfirmed. Press again to write them without P2P
bar.empty: Waiting for QSOs from the logger. When a P2P candidate shows up, answer yes / no here or type the park reference.
done.fail.title: Recording stopped, but the file could not be written
done.fail.body: You can build it again from “Upload files”.
spots.title: Activating now
spots.hint: pota.app spots are refreshed every minute. A station's parks are the spot's reference plus park references in the comment (“2fer JP-1206” etc.); a station spotted from another park within 15 minutes is listed as a 2fer.
build.title: Build upload files
build.file.hint: A file exported from your logger as ADIF
build.hint.all: All of them unless you pick some
build.acts.waiting: Choose an ADIF file to list activations here.
build.acts.emptyApp: No activation QSOs received yet. Start recording on “On the air”; QSOs arriving from the logger will be listed here.
build.acts.emptyAdif: No QSOs with your park (MY_SIG_INFO) found. QSOs made while recording are picked up automatically.
build.online: Check P2P against the pota.app hunter log
build.override.hint: Only for days you forgot to put your park in the logger.
set.title: Logger link
set.lede: QSOs logged by your logger arrive over UDP. Formats: N1MM (RUMlogNG, N1MM Logger+, DXLog, …), WSJT-X (WSJT-X, JTDX), ADIF (JTAlert, GridTracker, Log4OM, …). The app detects the format of each packet.
set.name: Name
set.none: No listeners. Create one with “Add listener”.
set.howto.general.p: Any logger that can send QSOs over UDP. In the logger, find the “send QSOs over UDP / broadcast” setting, point it at 127.0.0.1 and the port of a listener here. Any of these formats is accepted:
set.howto.loggers.p:
• N1MM format (contactinfo XML): RUMlogNG (Preferences → UDP, Contact info as N1MM), N1MM Logger+ (Config → Broadcast Data → Contacts), DXLog, Win-Test, …
  • WSJT-X format: WSJT-X, JTDX (Settings → Reporting, UDP Server). Using multicast 224.0.0.1 lets other programs receive at the same time
  • ADIF: JTAlert, GridTracker, Log4OM, and anything else that sends ADIF records over UDP
set.howto.fwd.p: To pass the same data on to another program (OpsLog, …), put that program's address and port in the listener's “Forward to”. Packets are relayed unchanged.
set.howto.dup.h: When the same QSO arrives on two listeners
set.howto.dup.p: A WSJT-X QSO arrives twice: from WSJT-X itself and again from the logger that received it. Same callsign, same band, same mode and less than 3 minutes apart counts as one contact, so keeping both listeners on never doubles anything. P2P decisions and deletions apply to both copies. The flip side: two contacts with the same station on the same band and mode within 3 minutes also become one.
upd.install.swap: It will be downloaded, swapped in and restarted.
upd.install.dl: It will be downloaded to your Downloads folder.
upd.modal.title: A new version is available
upd.manual: The new app was placed at {path}. Quit this app, move it to your Applications folder and open it.
b.hunterFail: ! Could not fetch the pota.app hunter log ({err}). Using saved data only.
b.noActivation: No activation QSOs found (needs MY_SIG_INFO, a recorded session, or “Override my park”).
b.note.unconfirmed: {date} {time} {call}: spotted from {parks}, but not confirmed while on the air, so not P2P
b.note.hunterWins: {date} {time} {call}: hunter log says {hunter}; {extra} from log/spots not used
b.note.hunterOverridesNo: {date} {time} {call}: marked “not P2P” on the air, but their hunter log has {hunter}, so it is P2P
b.note.twofer: {date} {time} {call}: {parks} were spotted separately around the same time, treated as a 2fer (could be a rover)
b.note.missing: {date} {time} {call} {band} {park}: in the pota.app hunter log but not in your log (call or time differs?)

terms.title: Terms of use and disclaimer
terms.body:
This app is hobby software by an individual, provided as is, without warranty, under the MIT License.

  • The author accepts no liability for any damage arising from the use of this app, including uploading wrong data to pota.app, duplicated or missing QSOs, lost logs or files, and effects on your logger or network settings. Always check the files before you upload them.
  • P2P and 2fer detection is an estimate based on pota.app spots and hunter logs; correctness is not guaranteed.
  • This app is not affiliated with Parks on the Air® (POTA) or pota.app; it only uses the public API. Follow pota.app's rules and upload requirements at all times.
  • Received QSOs, spot records and settings stay on this computer and are not sent anywhere. The app contacts api.pota.app for spots and GitHub to check for updates.
  • By continuing to use the app you agree to these terms.
